content:
Hi, I'm trying out the verso-slides genre, which looks really nice so far! I can't seem to figure out paths for including images. I've been trying out this which I saw in one of the examples on the repo:

:::stretch
![image](img/myimage.png)
:::

but it seems like that doesn't work if img is at the project root, nor does it work with ../img/myimage.png (the relative path from the .lean file as well as the index.html file in _slides. If I look at the generated html file it also produces the tag that should work (I'd thought): 

<img src="../img/myimage.png" alt="image">

but it only displays the alt image, maybe because it's going outside of the _slides folder and then the python html server sandboxes it? Is there a way to include these files?

it works if I make a symlink in _slides, e.g. 

ln -s /path/to/my/img _slides/img

but that feels pretty hacky

I agree! This is a known limitation at the moment.

The right solution is to have it locate the image with a source-file-relative path (because that's predictable) and then place it along with the HTML while building. I'll try to get that implemented soon. In the meantime, I'm glad you found a temporary workaround.

The issue with images should now be thoroughly resolved.

Instead of using the Markdown-style syntax, use {image "../foo.png"}[alt text]. This does the following:

  1. Resolves the image filename relative to the source file, rather than relative to some unspecified output dir
  2. Copies the image to the right place while building the HTML
  3. Allows width, height, and class parameters to control CSS for the image, e.g. {image "../foo.png" (width:=50%)}[alt]

I hope this works well for you.
